title: Atlas API Rails v1
claim: Semantic/API interpreters can emit one canonical classification packet that a deterministic Python rail validates, beacons into stable subsystem records, and recombines into a single Atlas record without reclassifying the same primitive for each view.
assumptions: Source document hashes and source spans are preserved before semantic extraction.
Python validation does not promote semantic inference into truth or canon.
definitions: Beacon: a stable JSON projection of one canonical subsystem block with a manifest hash.

Combined Atlas record: the canonical recomposition of identity, source, Nabla, Periodic-15, atom stack, warrant, dynamics, orientation, bridges, Reality Mirror, audit, and deterministic computed fields.
API rail: the deterministic Python boundary that validates and routes semantic/API output.
negative_guards: Python does not invent object type, claim family, bridge meaning, external-anchor meaning, or aggregate standing.
Candidate and Admitted graph state are never silently merged.
Marker 12 is never fabricated by the rail.
Aggregate Nabla semantics are flagged for semantic adjudication rather than guessed.
kill_conditions: The rail cannot round-trip a valid semantic packet into beacons and a combined record without loss of canonical object identity or source-span provenance.
Two beacons representing the same canonical primitive diverge semantically after recombination.

ledger.meaning: Deterministic emit/combine rails were added for API classification packets.
ledger.limits: No claim of successful runtime execution is made until fixture/regression receipts exist.
